title: The Stretch of a Healthy Options Card Record Looked At for a Recovery
content:
Where money is being put back onto a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card because another payer has met a dental, vision or hearing cost, how far back the card's own record is read is settled by the card's dispute window and by whether the card has been used at such a provider at all.

| Where the card's record shows | The stretch of the card's record looked at |
|---|---|
| the card gives the member 90 days or more to question a purchase, and the card has been used at a dental, vision or hearing provider | runs back 4 whole months from the day the money going back is worked out |
| the card gives the member 75 days or more to question a purchase, and the card has been used at a dental, vision or hearing provider | runs back 3 whole months from the day the money going back is worked out |
| in every other case | is the whole of the benefit year to date |

**The same, clause by clause.** The stretch of the card's record that is looked at runs back 4 whole months where the card is one that gives the member 90 days or more to question a purchase and the card has been used at a dental, vision or hearing provider; it runs back 3 whole months where the card is one that gives the member 75 days or more to question a purchase and the card has been used at such a provider; and in every other case it is the whole of the benefit year to date.

**How the two conditions are read.** The days a card gives the member to question a purchase is the dispute window that card's tier carries. Whether the card has been used at a dental, vision or hearing provider is read from the card's own entries: one purchase at such a provider is enough to satisfy it, whatever became of that purchase afterwards.

**Points of judgement, on hypothetical cards.** A card carrying a dispute window of 90 calendar days that shows one purchase at an optician: the first row is satisfied, and the stretch runs back 4 whole months. A card carrying a window of 75 calendar days showing a dental purchase: the first row is not satisfied and the second is, so the stretch runs back 3 whole months. A card carrying a window of 60 calendar days, whatever its entries: neither of the first two rows is satisfied, so the stretch is the whole of the benefit year to date. A card carrying a window of 90 calendar days but no purchase at any such provider: neither is satisfied, and again the stretch is the whole of the benefit year to date.
